blocks.text: tini is a minimal init that runs as PID 1, forwards signals to its child, and reaps zombies; your app runs as PID 2 with normal signal semantics.
$ docker run --init rag-api                       # Docker injects its bundled tini

blocks.code:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tini && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"]
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

blocks.text: Baking it into the image is most portable: Kubernetes has no `--init`.

rows: Server with SIGTERM handler, no children
Fix with `exec "$@"`; tini is still fine

blocks.text: tini signals only its direct child. If that child is a shell that started the app without exec, the app still misses SIGTERM. Use `tini -g` (process group) or dumb-init, or fix the script.

Q: "When do you need tini?" A: "When PID 1 would otherwise be a process that doesn't handle signals or reap children, such as custom scripts or apps that spawn subprocesses. Bake it in with ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"] so it works on every runtime, not just docker run --init."

items: tini only signals its direct child unless -g.
Servers with handlers and no children can skip it.
